newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet buy drains Italian Treasury war chest.
newsitem.headline: Stet buy drains Italian Treasury war chest.

text.p: The Italian Treasury's amortisation fund, a "war chest" used to buy back government debt, began this year with only 13 trillion lire cash, ministerial sources and analysts said.

The fund, meant to be financed by income from state sell-offs, has been drained of 3.0 trillion lire in the operation by which the Treasury takes over state industrial holding IRI 's controlling stake in telecoms holding Stet ahead of its planned privatisation.
Also, on December 31 the fund spent 600 billion lire in a buyback of Treasury certificates (CCTs) via the Bank of Italy.
The transfer of IRI's stake in Stet means the Treasury will have to pay out at least 14.53 trillion lire by the end of June, less the 3.0 trillion already handed over.
By February, some 8.4 trillion lire should flow into the fund from the sale of a second tranche of energy group ENI shares.
This will leave a negative balance of around 3.0 trillion lire which, the analysts said, could be covered by income from new privatisations.
In 1996 the Treasury, apart from the 3.0 trillion lire used for Stet, used some 13.3 trillion lire of the fund for the repurchase and redemption of state paper.
